root_cause: The code introduced in the LCEVC extradata support used a 32-bit signed int to hold a payload size read via a multi-byte/variable length decoder (get_mb, uint64_t) without validating that the value fits within range before using it in pointer/length arithmetic, allowing signed integer overflow and a negative computed block_size to bypass the sanity check that only guarded against overly large (not negative) sizes.
findings: In write_lcevc_nalu(), payload_size is declared as a plain 'int' but can be populated from get_mb(), which returns a uint64_t multi-byte-encoded value that can be arbitrarily large (up to 70 bits of accumulated data). When assigned to the int payload_size, the value truncates/overflows and can become negative or otherwise attacker-controlled in ways that break the subsequent arithmetic. block_size
